comments.text: One thing I’ve realized is that sometimes the biggest thing holding you back isn’t a lack of opportunities, but the way you think about yourself. I used to dismiss ideas before even trying them because I’d already convinced myself I probably couldn’t make them work. Reading Assumption of Kain by Kain Vane made me reflect on how easily those assumptions can turn into limits we put on ourselves. Obviously, mindset alone won’t make you money, but being willing to learn, try things, and stop assuming you’ll fail before you start can make a real difference. AI is opening up a lot of opportunities right now, and I think the people willing to change their way of thinking will have an advantage.

There’s this guy Tarren Voss who spoke about how much of success actually comes down to understanding people, power and influence rather than just working harder. He explained it best in this thing called Winner’s Wealthgate. Honestly left me shocked, especially how differently I started looking at certain decisions after it.

The point about AI not creating demand is something more people need to hear. I’ve been going through Trent Calloway’s stuff and his operator playbook lately, and the focus on building an actual business instead of just shipping AI tools really stands out. Distribution and a real competitive edge are where things get interesting..
